While I made this subreddit a few days ago I'll be posting regularly from now onward. I want to practice writing.

You might be wondering who in fact I'm talking to, and to be honest I don't exactly know. I've always had a feeling that my thoughts aren't exclusive or private. I don't know who you are, how many of y'all there are or why y'all are here. I'm going to just use y'all, and my imagination of your mannerisms and nuances to bounce ideas off of and to help clear my cluttered thoughts. That being said I'd like to propose that I'm a bit fucked in the head. Not enough to be committed anywhere (I hope), but just enough that it's recognizable to myself that some screws are definitely loose up in my noggin.

Somethings that have been increasingly concerning are things like depression, the call of the Void, and drug habits. I think I'm depressed similarly to Joaquin Phoenix in Her (2014) in that I distance myself emotionally from humanity. It's not like I dislike people, I've got a metric fuckton of friends, it's just that I find it hard to put effort into relationships of any kind. I sort of live in perpetual darkness. I wake up before the sun rises (if I'm not up already, but we'll get to that), I'll ride the tram downtown just as it lightens a smidge, walk an underground pathway all the way to school, be stuck in a windowless classroom for hours on end, and then do the reverse and get home well after dark to sit in my room with the lights out and the curtains drawn. I'll watch movies or TV shows or read books on my eReader or scroll through reddit for hours on end. My phone'll ring, usually one of my closer friends asking me to come and hang out, but I'll let it go to voicemail because any motion would take so much effort and I don't want to lie or make excuses to get out of whatever it is. Sometimes I forget to eat anything other than breakfast, and drink any water at all. I only figured this out when I tried using MyFitnessPal and I set a goal of 1400 calories daily and never hit even close.

So how'd I get to this point? Well, I guess it's a bunch of things that started a whole ago. I could probably pinpoint the day: February 2nd, 2014. It was the Saturday before my birthday and I was sitting in my rust bucket beater with my high school sweetheart girlfriend of almost 2 years. We were parked in a lot just 'round the bend of her house and she said, "I'm not happy." She made some reason up for not being happy with herself and whatnot but I knew a breakup line when I heard one.

We didn't talk much since then. I don't hate her for it, I just wish I could forget the look of pity in her eyes. Like she knew, somehow, I'd be so much worse without her. And to honest, I think I am. And to be a bloody lot depressing, I think she was the one I let slip. Lots of people say the line: there's 3.5 billion girls out there, you'll find your one. I'm worried I found mine and now she doesn't want me and never will again. Oh well, can't do shit about it now, now can I?

It's not like I haven't dated around since, more precisely slutted around really. I can't bring myself to emotionally invest in another person who could hurt me again. Trust issues and what not.

It's worse when I'm a decent actor and have quite a bit of walls around me. Everyone I've met out of high school would think I've always been the way I seem: outgoing, bouncy, personable, social butterfly - like. It's mostly a mask I've gotten used to wearing. People won't think to ask the hard hitting questions when they (a) don't know there's anything wrong or (b) think they know everything because I've perfected the skill of answering just thoroughly enough to satisfy any inquisitive /caring person but just short of my real thoughts. I'll offer up any answer to any question a person can answer, and in that way I ensure no one asks the right questions.

Cheers for now, need to be up in 2 hours.
